destination.title: Abelian charges and global gauge groups
destination.question: How do sections, charge data and geometric constructions determine abelian spectra and global gauge groups, and which completeness or charge bounds follow under specified assumptions?
destination.summary: Separates charge diagnostics, large-charge constructions, global quotients and completeness hypotheses.

regimes: Massless, light and full spectra distinguished
assumptions: Massless-only quotient and singlet-normalization hypotheses are questions to test
conventions: Primitive normalization and spectator sectors matter
Mordell–Weil torsion is not identified automatically with a discrete gauge factor
excludes: A universal massless-spectrum theorem inferred from examples

readingCoverage.readingLimit: The 2019 excerpt presents a universal massless-center statement as a hypothesis. Its separate discussion of singlet normalization supplies concerns, not a constructed F-theory counterexample.

sources.title: On $E_8$ and F-Theory GUTs

evidence.text: Can E8, suitably extended beyond its adjoint spectrum, organize the Abelian symmetries and matter charges of global F-theory SU(5) GUTs whose spectra need not admit ordinary adjoint Higgsing embeddings?

sources.title: F-theory and All Things Rational: Surveying U(1) Symmetries with Rational Sections

evidence.text: Which rational-section configurations in codimension-two fibers permit which U(1) matter charges in F-theory, particularly for SU(5) fundamental, antisymmetric and singlet matter? Can the singlet configurations organize Higgsing to discrete gauge symmetries?

sources.title: The Global Gauge Group Structure of F-theory Compactification with U(1)s

evidence.text: Do geometrically correlated U(1) charges determine a central quotient of the F-theory gauge group, and can the resulting restrictions be recognized from an effective theory's particle spectrum?

sources.title: Large U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: Determine the largest massless charge in six-dimensional F-theory with one U(1) factor, accounting for charge normalization and spectator gauge symmetry. Anomaly cancellation permits apparently unlimited spectra, while the source invokes geometric finiteness to motivate an upper bound.

sources.title: High U(1) charges in type IIB models and their F-theory lift

evidence.text: How can perturbative type IIB realize a single massless U(1) with highly charged massless matter, and how can its brane geometry guide F-theory constructions and possible charge bounds?

evidence.text: Does the center action on massless matter universally determine the global gauge group in F-theory?

evidence.text: How does F-theory geometry enforce charge completeness for connected gauge groups, and when do massless states alone generate the full charge lattice and determine the global gauge group?

sources.title: Orders of vanishing and U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: Can the absolute U(1) charge at a matter locus be inferred from vanishing orders of rational-section components in an unresolved elliptic fibration?

sources.title: Orders of vanishing and U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: The local example compares valuations for an elliptic curve with potential good reduction and its good-reduction transform after a ramified extension. These arithmetic quantities are subsequently related heuristically to the vanishing of a generating section at a matter locus.

sources.title: Orders of vanishing and U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: Which massless U(1) charge spectra occur in F-theory compactifications, beyond satisfying known low-energy consistency conditions? The paper seeks a geometric diagnostic that could help distinguish realizable spectra from an infinite set of candidate six-dimensional spectra.

sources.title: Orders of vanishing and U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: Can orders of vanishing of rational-section components determine massless U(1) charges without resolving the fibration, providing a Katz–Vafa analogue and predicting geometry for desired charge spectra?

sources.title: On $E_8$ and F-Theory GUTs

evidence.text: Use integer Higgs-charge matrices and Smith normal form with unimodular basis changes to determine surviving continuous charges and finite factors. Redundancy reduction uses computer scanning with some analytic checks.

sources.title: F-theory and All Things Rational: Surveying U(1) Symmetries with Rational Sections

evidence.text: Combines normal-bundle splitting on P1, normal-bundle exact sequences and divisor intersections. The central relation is D·C=−2−deg(N_C/D) for a smooth rational curve inside a smooth divisor of a smooth Calabi–Yau. Fiber adjacency and preserved intersection sums then restrict wrapping configurations.

sources.title: The Global Gauge Group Structure of F-theory Compactification with U(1)s

evidence.text: Tune b2 to zero in the specified Morrison–Park-type hypersurface, read the enhanced algebra and matter from the discriminant, and match a Higgs branching. Reject a simple ordinary-Higgs interpretation when the tuned geometry develops non-minimal loci.

sources.title: Large U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: The source presents hand-computable branching formulas and reports additional LieART calculations for many specific spectra. Those author-reported software checks are distinct from the manual algebra reconstructed here; no independent LieART execution or supplied code is available.

sources.title: High U(1) charges in type IIB models and their F-theory lift

evidence.text: Matrix factorizations of ξ²−b2, with b2=s6²/4−sL sR, and their reduced tensor powers construct divisors that split on X. Differences of conjugate divisor classes give integer multiples nD−.

sources.title: Generic matter representations in 6D supergravity theories

evidence.text: Match anomaly contributions with signed multiplicities, compensate dimensions with singlets, and inspect the neutral gain. Physical transitions additionally require available fields and a path in moduli space; anomaly equivalence alone establishes neither.

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Abelian and Discrete Symmetries in F-theory

evidence.text: How do global structures of elliptic and genus-one fibrations encode continuous and discrete abelian gauge symmetries, global gauge groups, charge constraints and particle-physics constructions in F-theory?

sources.title: Orders of vanishing and U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: How is massless charged matter encoded by an elliptic Calabi–Yau fibration? Nonabelian gauge factors arise along singular-fiber divisors, while the proposed abelian diagnostic uses rational sections at codimension-two matter loci.

sources.title: Orders of vanishing and U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: Can the proposed diagnostic recover a nontrivial abelian charge spectrum directly from a singular Weierstrass construction? The example tunes Morrison–Park coefficients over a surface and supplies a generating section for this test.

sources.title: Automatic enhancement in 6D supergravity and F-theory models

evidence.text: Can a higher-charge, non-UFD construction realize the fixed T=1 charge-one/charge-two spectrum while avoiding the enhancement seen in Morrison–Park form? Zero intersection of the two charge-three-supporting divisors is chosen to remove charge-three matter.

sources.title: Abelian F-theory Models with Charge-3 and Charge-4 Matter

evidence.text: How can U(1) F-theory models with charge-3 and charge-4 matter be constructed systematically, and what distinguishes their section and Weierstrass structures from lower-charge models?

sources.title: The Global Gauge Group Structure of F-theory Compactification with U(1)s

evidence.text: How do sections, exceptional divisors, and fibral curves encode the abelian generators, non-abelian Cartan algebra, and charged matter of F-theory compactifications?

evidence.text: Can six-dimensional generic representation types motivate common matter in four-dimensional F-theory?

sources.title: Modular Curves and Mordell-Weil Torsion in F-theory

evidence.text: Which Mordell-Weil torsion groups occur on smooth elliptically fibered Calabi-Yau varieties, and what restrictions follow for non-simply connected F-theory gauge groups and certain quotient torsors?

sources.title: Flopping and slicing: SO(4) and Spin(4)-models

evidence.text: How do crepant resolutions of colliding elliptic-fiber singularities engineer Spin(4) and SO(4), and determine their flop phases, topological invariants, matter content and six-dimensional anomaly cancellation?

sources.title: Large U(1) charges in F-theory

evidence.text: Can other Higgsings, exceptional groups, singular parents or compactification frameworks yield larger primitive charges? Can these Weierstrass constructions support actual four-dimensional vacua after flux and superpotential conditions are imposed?

sources.title: The Global Gauge Group Structure of F-theory Compactification with U(1)s

evidence.text: Does the quotient derived from geometric massless states extend to massive states and strongly coupled sectors? Can singlet-lattice completeness be proved, and can the same global data constrain discrete Higgs phases or connect to weak-gravity conditions?

evidence.text: Which massless scalar charges can compensate the dilaton-dependent anomalous-U(1) FI term?

evidence.text: How can rational elliptic fourfolds and their double covers systematically generate four-dimensional N = 1 F-theory geometries with multiple section-derived U(1) factors, and can base geometry indicate compatible K3 fibrations and heterotic duals?

evidence.text: Can a bounded SU(5) charge-spectrum search be replaced by a reusable Lean formalization whose witness, completion, and closure theorems certify exactly the spectra satisfying specified selection-rule and completeness requirements?

evidence.text: Can an explicit parameterized Weierstrass construction realize the directly tuned Standard Model quotient gauge group with generic matter, and capture all allowed moduli for fixed gauge and divisor data?

evidence.text: How can projective duality classify maximal-rank singularities of rational elliptic 1/2 Calabi–Yau threefolds, expose their fibers and sections, and determine geometric inputs for six-dimensional N=1 F-theory on their double covers?

evidence.text: When can complex-structure tuning make a free rational section torsional, enhancing a U(1) to a non-simply-connected gauge group? How does a related bisection geometry with a torsional Jacobian fit the F-theory interpretation?

evidence.text: How large can charges of massless or light fields become under a U(1) in four-dimensional F-theory, particularly a U(1) decoupled from other gauge sectors? The paper constructs large-charge examples and asks whether their charges approach a landscape upper bound.

evidence.text: Construct a six-dimensional N=(1,0) F-theory model with Mordell–Weil torsion Z4⊕Z4, determine its gauge group and matter, and investigate its relation to charge completeness, stable degeneration and a heterotic dual.

evidence.text: How different can a genus-one fibered Calabi–Yau threefold be from its Jacobian, especially in topology and non-Abelian gauge symmetry? Can twisted circle reductions explain such differences among geometries described as CY torsors?

sources.title: Calabi-Yau Genus-One Fibrations and Twisted Dimensional Reductions of F-theory

evidence.text: Use a toric reflexive-polytope construction and the Batyrev formula to obtain Hodge numbers. A quartic fiber equation, Stanley–Reisner ideal and restrictions to divisors identify fibral components and their monodromy.

sources.title: Calabi-Yau Genus-One Fibrations and Twisted Dimensional Reductions of F-theory

evidence.text: Shrink the g1 fiber component, then apply the Jacobian map to obtain Weierstrass coefficients. The displayed leading discriminant is Δ = f1^6 D4,Z + O(f1^7); its fiber interpretation is used to infer the Jacobian gauge symmetry.

sources.title: Calabi-Yau Genus-One Fibrations and Twisted Dimensional Reductions of F-theory

evidence.text: Interpret monodromy through foldings of affine Dynkin diagrams, and infer gauge rank from fibral divisors. The review also describes the elliptic divisor decomposition into pulled-back base divisors, fibral divisors, the zero-section and free Mordell–Weil generators.
